Nine Squares: What Is This About?

AlgebraAreaInvariants
Game: Nine squares sit side by side and change size as you slide a number. Find out which ones refuse to change, and find the one setting where they fit together perfectly.
How to play: Move the slider for a. Watch the small black square and the two red ones, and look for the setting with no gaps and no overlaps.

    Look for the math

    Seven of the nine squares change with a, yet the black square and the two red ones stay exactly the same size. Is that a coincidence?

    Why the red square is always 4

    Call the side of the blue square a and the side of the red square in the middle c. The other sides follow from the picture. Adding the three squares along the top gives a + (a + 1) + (a + 1 + c) = 3a + 2 + c. Adding the three along the bottom gives (a + 1 + 2c) + (a - 2) + (a - 1) = 3a - 2 + 2c. The two rows are the same width, so c = 4, whatever a is. The test confirms that the rows agree for exactly one value of c, and that the red 4 and the red 15 never change. The same kind of argument fixes the other red square at 15.

    A rectangle of unequal squares

    The picture only closes up when everything fits. The test checked every a from 3 to 500 and found that the squares have no gaps and no overlaps for a = 9 alone. Then the sides are 1, 4, 7, 8, 9, 10, 14, 15 and 18, all different, and they fill a 33 by 32 rectangle (area 1056, the sum of their squares). This perfect rectangle was found by Zbigniew Morón in 1925. Nine is the fewest squares for which this is possible.

    Can a square be done too?

    Cutting a square into squares that are all different is much harder. The page lists Sprague's 55 pieces (1939) and a 24-piece square from 1948, and says that the record has held since. That is out of date: in 1978 A. J. W. Duijvestijn found a square of side 112 cut into 21 different squares, and a computer search showed that no smaller number can do it.

    Slide a up from 3 and watch the squares first overlap, then leave gaps. Stop when the picture is a clean rectangle.
